title: ProperOpenInterchange reduction Square
statement: Under the original proper/open hypotheses and intermediate admissibility, Assertion holds for properOpenInterchange Gamma on endpoint words of length at most three, without a length bound on the additional restriction of the proper target word. The normalized operation models are those of [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge] and the typed-word domain is that of [def-sf-integral-system-expression-domain]; the operation data, finite words, generator kinds, admissibility predicates and the coefficient-square Assertion are those of [def-sf-generator-reduction-data]. This is only this forward generator case; it asserts neither the other three generators nor inverse-square or naturality clauses. StructuralSquares is the predicate of [def-sf-open-interchange-reduction-data].

source.place: Open-adjunction and clopen calculations, corresponding generator case.

proof.text:
Write $T=\mathcal R$ and abbreviate the asserted square for $a:B\to C$ by $a r_B=r_C T(a_{\rm int})$. Squares paste: for $b:C\to D$, $(ba)r_B=b r_C T(a_{\rm int})=r_D T(b_{\rm int}a_{\rm int})$. They pass to inverses: multiply the square for an isomorphism $a$ by $a^{-1}$ on the left and $T(a_{\rm int}^{-1})$ on the right. For an outer unary operation $A$, naturality of $r_A$ and $r_{AB}=A(r_B)r_A$ give
$$A(a)r_{AB}=A(a r_B)r_A=A(r_C)r_A T(A_{\rm int}(a_{\rm int}))=r_{AC}T(A_{\rm int}(a_{\rm int})).$$
At a tensor vertex the same substitution in each slot uses naturality of $r_\otimes$ and its defining binary recursion. Induction on the number of outer vertices proves this for any finite context in the stated typed domain. This is only closure of already established squares; it asserts no new reconstruction or preservation result.

proof.text:
For the cartesian open square put $F=P_g$, $F_U=P_{g_U}$ and $\theta:P_{j'}F\cong F_UP_j$. The open normalization gives
$$\beta_M^{-1}=\epsilon^o_{FJ_jM}\circ J_{j'}(\theta^{-1}\circ F_U(u^o_M)),$$
Equivalently the arrow being transposed is $F_UM\xrightarrow{F_Uu^o_M}F_UP_jJ_jM\xrightarrow{\theta^{-1}}P_{j'}FJ_jM$. Its integral version is the identical word in the independently specified integral maps. The square for $\theta^{\pm1}$ follows by pasting the two pullback compositors and their inverses, since the scheme square and its coefficient ring maps commute. The open-unit and open-counit squares are hypotheses. Thus step 1 applied to this displayed adjunct word gives the square for $\beta^{-1}$, and inversion gives it for $\beta$.

proof.text: The restriction/tensor identification $t_j:P_j(H\otimes N)\cong P_jH\otimes P_jN$ also has its coefficient square, including the completed integral interpretation. Here is the representative check needed for this assertion. Use flat-term K-flat representatives and the quotient-tensor models for restriction and tensor. Both orders send a homogeneous tensor $x\otimes y$ at quotient $n$ to $(1\otimes j^*x)\otimes(1\otimes j^*y)$. For completed tensor the recorded completion map has precisely this first Roos coordinate and zero shifted coordinate; restriction carries these coordinates to the same coordinates. The maps commute with $A_m\to A_n$ because restriction preserves the coefficient projections and sends $1$ to $1$. Their differentials agree: both send the $(a,b)$ summand by $d x\otimes y+(-1)^a x\otimes d y$. Thus this is an equality of maps of strict quotient complexes, with the actual completion comparison, not just an equality after evaluated derived reduction. The immersion comparison identifies completed restriction with this ordinary restriction. The representative-normalized bridge and tensor descent carry the equality to the specified whole-system derived square. Inversion gives the square for $t_j^{-1}$.

proof.text:
Put $H=J_jM\otimes N$. By the open normalization, $\gamma^{-1}:J_j(M\otimes P_jN)\to H$ is
$$\epsilon^o_H\circ J_j\bigl(t_j^{-1}\circ(u^o_M\otimes1)\bigr).$$
The normalization applies both to the completed coefficient ring and to the ringed diagram topos of strict systems. These are the canonical integral and system arrows in the statement. Step 3 supplies the restriction/tensor square, the assumed open-unit and counit squares supply the other factors, and step 1 supplies their tensor whiskerings and composite. This proves the square for $\gamma^{-1}$ and hence for $\gamma$. The specified $r_j$ is the canonical simultaneous quotient open-tensor map, so this calculation uses the given comparison rather than a separately chosen open realization.

proof.text:
For the square $Q$, the proper/open lemma supplies the clopen lift $s$ and the stipulated four-factor expression for $\lambda_Q$. Let $d:J_bJ_s\cong J_k$ be the canonical open compositor. Its inverse is the left-adjoint conjugate of the restriction compositor $P_sP_b\cong P_k$: if $L_1=J_k$, $R_1=P_k$, $L_2=J_bJ_s$, $R_2=P_sP_b$ and $\delta:R_2\cong R_1$ is that restriction compositor, then $d^{-1}=\epsilon_{1,L_2}\circ L_1(\delta L_2)\circ L_1(\eta_2)$ for the composite open adjunction. Thus its formula uses only open units, open counits and that pullback compositor. The stated open-unit normalization fixes this choice of $d$, in both coefficient categories. By the assumed structural squares and step 1, $d$ and $d^{-1}$ have their coefficient squares. The normalized open restriction factor is explicitly
$$z:P_bJ_k\longrightarrow J_s,\qquad z=(u^o_{b,J_s})^{-1}\circ P_b(d^{-1}).$$
It follows that $z$ has its coefficient square. This also identifies the canonical $P_bJ_k\cong J_s$ used in the four-factor formula without introducing a choice of an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Write $L_1=P_pJ_i$, $R_1=P_iS_p$, $L_2=J_bP_q$, $R_2=S_qP_b$ with the composite adjunctions. The first factor $c:R_1\cong R_2$ is the conjugate of $\beta^{-1}:L_2\cong L_1$, hence
$$c=R_2(\epsilon_1)\circ R_2(\beta^{-1})R_1\circ\eta_2R_1.$$
Composite units and counits have the formulas $G(\eta_H)\circ\eta_F$ and $\epsilon_H\circ H(\epsilon_F)$ for $HF\dashv GI$. Consequently every factor in this displayed word has a square: step 2 supplies $\beta^{-1}$, and the hypotheses supply the basic units and counits; step 1 supplies their whiskerings and pastings. The same composite-adjunction formulas define $c_{\rm int}$ through the canonical bridge. This proves the square for the first factor, using conjugation of the open comparison, without applying any proper-base-change theorem.

proof.text:
The clopen comparison $h_s:J_s\cong S_s$ in the specified formula is
$$h_s=S_s((u^o_s)^{-1})\circ\eta_{s,J_s}:J_s\longrightarrow S_sP_sJ_s\longrightarrow S_s.$$
The proper/open lemma identifies this with the clopen section comparison; its integral counterpart is the same unit/inverse-unit composite by the bridge. The assumed $P_s\dashv S_s$ unit square and $J_s\dashv P_s$ open-unit square, inversion, and step 1 therefore prove the square for $h_s$. Clopenness supplies invertibility; it does not supply an unstated claim that arbitrary extension by zero commutes with direct image.

proof.text:
Now write the four factors with their actual domains:
$$P_iS_pJ_k\xrightarrow{cJ_k}S_qP_bJ_k\xrightarrow{S_qz}S_qJ_s\xrightarrow{S_qh_s}S_qS_s\xrightarrow{a_{q,s}}S_r.$$
Steps 5--7 give the squares of the first three factors, after the whiskerings of step 1. The direct-image-compositor square is an explicit hypothesis, and $qs=r$. Pasting yields
$$\lambda_{Q,TK}\circ r_{P_iS_pJ_k}=r_{S_r}\circ T(\lambda_{Q,\rm int}).$$
All factors are isomorphisms by the cited proper/open statement, so step 1 also gives the inverse square. The argument uses the cartesian square defining $V_W$ only for the first open comparison; it never assumes that the original square $Q$ is cartesian. The hypotheses explicitly cover these intermediate words and the structural maps used to form their adjoints, rather than only the length-three endpoints.

proof.text:
Finally $\Gamma_Q=\epsilon^o\circ J_i(\lambda_Q^{-1})$, and the integral arrow is the same open transpose. The inverse $\lambda$ square just proved, whiskered by $J_i$, and the assumed open-counit square paste to
$$\Gamma_{Q,TK}\circ r_{J_iS_r}=r_{S_pJ_k}\circ T(\Gamma_{Q,\rm int}).$$
Every equality above was obtained by naturality, functorial composition, or equality of the specified simultaneous chain maps before localization. They therefore hold in the ordinary derived category of whole semilinear systems and are natural in each input. Evaluation is not used to detect equality. The normalization, origin, constructibility and common amplitude requirements are exactly those stipulated for each intermediate, and no additional bound on the word length has been imposed.

theorem properOpenInterchangeReductionSquare
    {D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}} (Cf : D.CoefficientDatum)
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic Cf.l) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (Padic Cf.l) E] (o : Operations Cf.l E)
    (hStructural : StructuralSquares.{u, s, i} Cf.l E D o)
    {S : Type s} (W : S → Scheme.{u}) (hW : FiniteTypeFamily W D.k)
    {I : Type i} (location : I → S)
    {a b c d : S}
      (k : W a ⟶ W b) (r : W a ⟶ W c) (p : W b ⟶ W d) (i : W c ⟶ W d)
      (h : k ≫ p = r ≫ i) (hk : IsOpenImmersion k) (hki : QuasiCompact k)
      (hio : IsOpenImmersion i) (hii : QuasiCompact i)
      (hr : IsProper r) (hp : IsProper p) (B : Word W location a)
    (hSourceLength : (Word.open i hio hii (Word.push r (by let := hr; infer_instance)
          (by let := hr; infer_instance) (by let := hr; infer_instance) hr B)).length ≤ 3)
    (hTargetLength : (Word.push p (by let := hp; infer_instance) (by let := hp; infer_instance)
          (by let := hp; infer_instance) hp (Word.open k hk hki B)).length ≤ 3)
    (K : ∀ k : I, DerivedCategory (scalarReductionSource Cf.l E (W (location k))))
    (lo hi torLo torHi : ℤ)
    (hInputs : ∀ k : I, Admissible Cf.l E
      (IntegralSystemRealization.calculus Cf.l E (W (location k))) (K k)
      lo hi torLo torHi)
    (hSource : Word.admissible Cf.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi
      (Word.open i hio hii
      (Word.push r (by let := hr; infer_instance)
          (by let := hr; infer_instance) (by let := hr; infer_instance) hr B)))
    (hTarget : Word.admissible Cf.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi
      (Word.push p (by let := hp; infer_instance) (by let := hp; infer_instance)
          (by let := hp; infer_instance) hp (Word.open k hk hki B)))
    (hGenerator : GeneratorKind.admissible Cf.l E W location o K lo hi torLo torHi
      (GeneratorKind.properOpenInterchange k r p i h hk hki hio hii hr hp B)) :
    Assertion Cf.l E W location o K
      (GeneratorKind.properOpenInterchange k r p i h hk hki hio hii hr hp B)
